Both traces build the same two core structures: the four-slot block Holly→Cloth→1716→Palm and the chain Ash/Rag→1713→Vellum→1711→Maple. They diverge in how they mishandle the valid block-at-2-5 branch before recovering. Trace 1 initially discards Case 2 because of an indexing slip: it briefly treats slot 2 as needing Ash rather than slot 1, creating a false Ash/Holly conflict; later it re-evaluates and finds the candidate solution. Trace 2 initially treats the “left” clues as year-value inequalities, so Vellum in slot 4 with year 1716 seems impossible because 1716 < 1711; after correcting the chain to positional order, it recovers the same solution. The sibling trace confirms the payoff: both end with block at slots 2-5, Ash at 1, 1713 at 2, Vellum at 4, 1711 at 5, Maple at 6.

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Case 1: Block is at 1-2-3-4." end="Thus, Case 1 (Block at 1-4) is impossible." basis="Explores block placement 1-4 and explicitly rejects it because the Vellum/1711/Maple chain cannot fit after 1713; this pruning narrows later block placement."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Case 2: Block is at 2-3-4-5." end="So Case 2 (Block at 2-5) seems impossible given the Ash/1713 placement." basis="Opens the valid block placement and tries Ash positions, then discards it due to an Ash/Holly indexing slip; the pruning is later overturned but has visible downstream effect."
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Case 3: Block is at 3-4-5-6." end="So Case 3 is invalid." basis="Opens block placement 3-6 and eliminates it using clue 11 because 1716 would land in slot 5."
